sources.entry: ContainerDesk - Native SwiftUI workspace for Apple's container runtime, with live resource monitoring and an integrated terminal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/MacHatter1/ContainerDesk) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: ContainerDesk is a native macOS SwiftUI app for managing containers, images, volumes, networks and builds through Apple's `container` CLI, with live resource gauges, a built-in terminal and an optional local MLX AI playground.
summary.what_it_does: The app provides a single window for browsing and managing Apple container runtime resources: containers, images, volumes, networks, registries, machines, builds, Compose, Kubernetes, and system services. Containers show live CPU and memory against configured limits, and there are log viewers, stats charts with history, and an interactive shell per container. Users can group containers into local "stacks" and save reusable environment profiles for launches. A Cleanup screen scans for unused resources and removes only the reviewed candidates, without bulk prune commands. The Local AI section discovers MLX models, runs an app-owned MLX-LM server bound to 127.0.0.1, and offers a chat playground. Activity records command previews and exit codes, but not command output.
use_cases: manage Apple container runtime from a GUI
monitor CPU and memory of running containers on a Mac
open a shell inside a running container
clean up stopped containers and unused images safely
run a local MLX language model and chat with it
build images and manage local Compose or Kubernetes clusters
how_to_run: Install Apple's container CLI (from its releases page or Homebrew)
git clone <repository URL shown in README>
stack: Swift 6.2 or newer (to build from source)
notable: Native SwiftUI window covering containers, images, volumes, networks, builds, Compose and Kubernetes, with the Apple container CLI remaining the runtime authority
Live CPU and memory gauges against configured limits, with 15- and 60-minute stats history and threshold notifications
Cleanup scans and selects stopped containers and unused images/networks, leaves volumes opt-in, and removes each selected resource individually
Edit Limits recreates a container with new CPU/memory limits, with backup and recovery files
Local MLX server bound only to 127.0.0.1 with an OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint and in-memory chat
caveats: Requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 26 or later
Builds are not Developer ID signed or notarized, so Gatekeeper may block first launch
Edit Limits requires exactly CLI and API server 1.5.0 and APFS copy-on-write cloning; interrupted recreation requires manual recovery
Local MLX features only work with exactly MLX-LM 0.32.2; Python and MLX-LM must be installed separately
